lines.text: Pick any prime number bigger than three. Square it, then add seventeen.
lines.caption: Pick any prime number bigger than three. Square it, then add seventeen.

lines.text: Now divide by twelve. <short pause> The remainder is ALWAYS the same! But why?
lines.caption: Now divide by twelve. The remainder is ALWAYS the same! But why?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Let p be a prime greater than three.
lines.caption: Let p be a prime greater than three.

lines.text: What is the remainder when p squared plus seventeen is divided by twelve?
lines.caption: What is the remainder when p squared plus seventeen is divided by twelve?

lines.text: Is it zero, one, five, six, or eleven?
lines.caption: Is it zero, one, five, six, or eleven?

lines.text: A prime has exactly two factors, one and itself. Like five, seven, eleven and thirteen.
lines.caption: A prime has exactly two factors, one and itself. Like five, seven, eleven and thirteen.

lines.text: The remainder is what's left after taking out all the twelves. Twenty-six leaves two.
lines.caption: The remainder is what's left after taking out all the twelves. Twenty-six leaves two.

lines.text: We don't know p. So the answer must work for EVERY prime bigger than three.
lines.caption: We don't know p. So the answer must work for EVERY prime bigger than three.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our first strategy: try a few primes, and look for a pattern.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our first strategy: try a few primes, and look for a pattern.

lines.text: Start with five. Five squared is twenty-five. Plus seventeen is forty-two.
lines.caption: Start with five. Five squared is twenty-five. Plus seventeen is forty-two.

lines.text: That's three twelves, plus six.
lines.caption: That's three twelves, plus six.

lines.text: Next, seven. Seven squared is forty-nine. Plus seventeen is sixty-six.
lines.caption: Next, seven. Seven squared is forty-nine. Plus seventeen is sixty-six.

lines.text: That's five twelves, plus six. Six again!
lines.caption: That's five twelves, plus six. Six again!

lines.text: Eleven squared is one hundred twenty-one. Plus seventeen is one hundred thirty-eight.
lines.caption: Eleven squared is one hundred twenty-one. Plus seventeen is one hundred thirty-eight.

lines.text: That's eleven groups of twelve, plus six.
lines.caption: That's eleven groups of twelve, plus six.

lines.text: Thirteen squared is one hundred sixty-nine. Plus seventeen is one hundred eighty-six.
lines.caption: Thirteen squared is one hundred sixty-nine. Plus seventeen is one hundred eighty-six.

lines.text: That's fifteen groups of twelve, plus six.
lines.caption: That's fifteen groups of twelve, plus six.

lines.text: Six every time! So the answer is D.
lines.caption: Six every time! So the answer is D.

lines.text: Testing is a smart contest shortcut. But it isn't a proof. So WHY is it always six?
lines.caption: Testing is a smart contest shortcut. But it isn't a proof. So WHY is it always six?

lines.text: Here's another way. Let's write the numbers in rows of six.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Let's write the numbers in rows of six.

lines.text: A prime bigger than three isn't even, or two would divide it. Cross out columns two, four and six.
lines.caption: A prime bigger than three isn't even, or two would divide it. Cross out columns two, four and six.

lines.text: It isn't a multiple of three either. Cross out column three.
lines.caption: It isn't a multiple of three either. Cross out column three.

lines.text: Only columns one and five are left. Every prime bigger than three lands in them!
lines.caption: Only columns one and five are left. Every prime bigger than three lands in them!

lines.text: Not every number there is prime, like twenty-five. But every prime past three is there.
lines.caption: Not every number there is prime, like twenty-five. But every prime past three is there.

lines.text: That's why the question says bigger than three. Two and three got crossed out.
lines.caption: That's why the question says bigger than three. Two and three got crossed out.

lines.text: Column one is one after a multiple of six. Column five is one before.
lines.caption: Column one is one after a multiple of six. Column five is one before.

lines.text: So p is always one away from a multiple of six. Now let's look at p squared.
lines.caption: So p is always one away from a multiple of six. Now let's look at p squared.

lines.text: Take seven. Seven squared is forty-nine dots, in a seven by seven square.
lines.caption: Take seven. Seven squared is forty-nine dots, in a seven by seven square.

lines.text: Take away one corner dot. Then move the rest of the bottom row to the side.
lines.caption: Take away one corner dot. Then move the rest of the bottom row to the side.

lines.text: Now it's a rectangle: six rows by eight columns. That's forty-eight!
lines.caption: Now it's a rectangle: six rows by eight columns. That's forty-eight!

lines.text: Six and eight are the neighbors of seven, one below and one above.
lines.caption: Six and eight are the neighbors of seven, one below and one above.

lines.text: This works for every p. p squared minus one equals p minus one, times p plus one.
lines.caption: This works for every p. p squared minus one equals p minus one, times p plus one.

lines.text: One neighbor is a multiple of six. And p is odd, so the other neighbor is even.
lines.caption: One neighbor is a multiple of six. And p is odd, so the other neighbor is even.

lines.text: A multiple of six, times an even number, is a multiple of twelve!
lines.caption: A multiple of six, times an even number, is a multiple of twelve!

lines.text: So p squared is always a multiple of twelve, plus one. Seventeen is twelve plus five.
lines.caption: So p squared is always a multiple of twelve, plus one. Seventeen is twelve plus five.

lines.text: One plus five is six. The answer is six, for EVERY prime bigger than three!
lines.caption: One plus five is six. The answer is six, for EVERY prime bigger than three!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you need to be sure a pattern never breaks.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you need to be sure a pattern never breaks.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: One is the remainder of p squared alone. It forgets the seventeen.
lines.caption: One is the remainder of p squared alone. It forgets the seventeen.

lines.text: Five is the remainder of seventeen alone. It forgets p squared.
lines.caption: Five is the remainder of seventeen alone. It forgets p squared.

lines.text: Zero is what seven gives if you forget to square. Seven plus seventeen is twenty-four, two twelves.
lines.caption: Zero is what seven gives if you forget to square. Seven plus seventeen is twenty-four, two twelves.

lines.text: Eleven is the biggest remainder twelve allows. But we just showed it's always six.
lines.caption: Eleven is the biggest remainder twelve allows. But we just showed it's always six.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Find each part's remainder, add them, and take out any extra group of twelve.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Find each part's remainder, add them, and take out any extra group of twelve.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? p is still a prime bigger than three.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? p is still a prime bigger than three.

lines.text: What is the remainder when five times p squared, plus nine, is divided by twelve?
lines.caption: What is the remainder when five times p squared, plus nine, is divided by twelve?

lines.text: Use the same plan. Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Use the same plan. Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. p squared is a multiple of twelve, plus one.
lines.caption: Let's check. p squared is a multiple of twelve, plus one.

lines.text: Five copies of that make a multiple of twelve, plus five.
lines.caption: Five copies of that make a multiple of twelve, plus five.

lines.text: Five plus nine is fourteen. That's one more twelve, plus two. So the remainder is two!
lines.caption: Five plus nine is fourteen. That's one more twelve, plus two. So the remainder is two!

lines.text: Let's test with five. Five times twenty-five, plus nine, is one hundred thirty-four.
lines.caption: Let's test with five. Five times twenty-five, plus nine, is one hundred thirty-four.

lines.text: That's eleven groups of twelve, plus two. It matches!
lines.caption: That's eleven groups of twelve, plus two. It matches!

lines.text: If you found a remainder of two, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found a remainder of two, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea. Every prime bigger than three is one away from a multiple of six.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea. Every prime bigger than three is one away from a multiple of six.

lines.text: So its square always leaves one when divided by twelve. Use that, then add the rest.
lines.caption: So its square always leaves one when divided by twelve. Use that, then add the rest.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep asking why, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep asking why, and I'll see you next time!
